title: OpenAI Responses Proxy
question: How does OpenAI Responses Proxy make a Codex Responses turn portable across third-party providers, and how does it install its own listener and keep it running?
summary: A loopback listener rebuilds each Responses request in one closed grammar with store=false, sends it, within one total deadline, to the upstream that its path names, and retries only what the failure class allows. A signed release asset installs through one journaled transaction as an immutable generation; an upgrade hands the listening socket to a successor process, and a watchdog under the native service manager restarts a stopped listener.
scope: The OpenAI Responses Proxy product as released at v8.0.0: the openai_responses_proxy package, pyproject.toml and VERSION.

overview.lead: A loopback data plane for Codex and other Responses clients: each request is rebuilt store-free and sent to the upstream that its path names, and the proxy installs, hands off and supervises its own listener.

views.title: One Responses turn, from the client to a provider
views.question: Which components handle the turn on the way, and in what order?
views.summary: The loopback listener passes each turn to the Responses relay, which projects the body and admits it. The Upstream exchange sends it over the Upstream transport to the provider; Response delivery returns JSON or SSE.

views.title: What leaves the listener
views.question: What does the projection keep and remove, and how is a request the provider refuses made smaller?
views.summary: Replay projection sets store=false and removes the bindings to a previous response, a conversation and a cache, keeping calls paired with outputs. Bounded recovery re-projects strictly smaller, pair-safe requests derived from one the provider refused.

views.title: Failures bounded per upstream origin
views.question: After an upstream failure, what is retried and reported, and how is only its upstream origin cooled?
views.summary: The Upstream exchange retries only what the failure class allows and cools only its upstream origin on a 429 or a 503 after retries. Telemetry counts failure classes; the Upstream transport never resends a complete request left unanswered.

views.title: One install, one transaction
views.question: How does a signed release asset become the active generation, and how far back can a rollback go?
views.summary: Release admission verifies SHA256SUMS.sig, and the journaled Payload transaction materializes the admitted bytes as a new generation. It ends finalized, or the prior state is restored; the generation selector keeps at most one predecessor.

views.title: A new listener without a dropped turn
views.question: How do an upgrade and a reload move the listening socket to a successor process?
views.summary: Listener handoff passes the listening socket to a successor process, and request admission stays open throughout; no other transition exists. Deployment refuses a listener unless it declares both selected-generation-handoff and admission-preserving-handoff, and proves the successor's identity before the transaction finalizes.

views.title: Kept running by the operating system
views.question: When does the watchdog start the listener?
views.summary: Called by Lifecycle commands, Native supervision registers the watchdog with the native service manager and removes it on uninstall; the service manager starts and restarts it. When the watchdog finds the port closed, it starts the listener, but it waits while a transaction is open and not yet activated.
